title: Meditations
subtitle: The Classic George Long Translation – with Modern Commentary, a Guide to Stoic Living and a 30-Day Practice
author: Marcus Aurelius
pd_statement: The Meditations were written in Greek by the Roman emperor Marcus Aurelius (121–180). This edition uses the English translation by George Long (1801–1879), first published in 1862, which is in the public domain. Long’s wording is kept; his footnotes and his marks for uncertain passages are left out, and obvious printing errors are corrected.

sub: The Stoic classic with modern commentary

headline: Master your mind.
Accept what is.
Do what is right.
paras: Nearly two thousand years ago, the most powerful man in the world sat in a military camp on the Danube and wrote notes to himself – about anger and patience, duty and death, and how to stay good in a hard world. He never meant them to be read. Today they are one of the most loved books ever written.

This beautifully designed annotated edition presents the complete twelve books in George Long’s classic translation and adds what today’s reader needs to live them: a clear guide to Stoic ideas, a reflection and a practice after every book, and a guided 30-day Stoic practice.
